entry.speaker: Varn
entry.text: I stopped counting. The deaths. The returns. At some point the number becomes irrelevant and only the fact of it remains. You are here. I am here. The dungeon continues. That is all that is true.

responses.text: I've been thinking about what you said last time.
What do you want from this conversation?

gets_easier.speaker: Varn
gets_easier.text: No. It gets quieter. That is not the same thing. The noise — the certainty that things should be otherwise — that fades. What remains is just the loop, and whatever I choose to do inside it.

last_time.speaker: Varn
last_time.text: I said a great deal across many times. The versions blur together. But I am glad something held. That is more than the dungeon intended, I think.

responses.text: What do you choose to do, in the loop?

what_want.speaker: Varn
what_want.text: Honesty. I have had enough of the shapes we perform for each other — the warnings, the tasks, the rituals. I know you. You know me. Let us speak plainly while we still can.

what_choose.speaker: Varn
what_choose.text: Understanding. I know something about what watches this dungeon — what watches us, inside it. I am willing to share it. But I have a condition.

the_condition.speaker: Varn
the_condition.text: Tell me something true. Not about the dungeon. Not about me. About yourself. Something from these runs that you have not said aloud. I need to know you are still in there — that the loop has not hollowed you the way it has hollowed some of the things I have seen return here.

responses.text: I keep coming back because I don't know how to stop.
I'm not sure I'm the same person who started this.
I came back because of you. To understand what you became.

truth_compulsion.speaker: Varn
truth_compulsion.text: That is honest. More honest than I expected. The dungeon does that — removes the exits until the only direction is forward. I have wondered whether you stay because you choose to or because choice has been taken from you. Now I know: you do not know either. That is the most human thing I have heard in a very long time.

responses.text: Now tell me what you know.

truth_changed.speaker: Varn
truth_changed.text: No. Neither am I. That is the thing the dungeon takes that you do not notice losing — the fixed point of yourself that you navigate from. We are both drift, now. I find that less troubling than I once would have.

responses.text: Now tell me what you know.

truth_varn.speaker: Varn
truth_varn.text:
...

That will do. That is more than enough.

abaddon_reveal.speaker: Varn
abaddon_reveal.text: The dungeon is not empty at its deepest point. Something is there — has always been there. I felt it through the chains, before they broke. It does not sleep. It waits. It has been watching every run, every death, every return. It already knows your name.

responses.text: How long has it been watching?

abaddon_watching.speaker: Varn
abaddon_watching.text: Since before you arrived. Since before I was made Chainkeeper. The dungeon — the whole structure of it — was built around keeping that presence from reaching outward. I was the lock. You were the key that was never supposed to exist. I do not think that was an accident.

abaddon_wants.speaker: Varn
abaddon_wants.text: I do not know. That is the question I cannot answer, and I have had a great deal of time to try. Perhaps nothing. Perhaps everything. Perhaps it only wants to be seen. I have found that some things, when finally acknowledged, stop needing to be feared. I cannot promise that is true here.
